content: I'm adding @Chris Birkbeck here who developed the mathlib quality Claude code optimisation tool @Bolton Bailey and @Alexander Hicks are using (in case people want to connect, discuss or give feedback/ask questions)

Thanks for making this tool Chris, I guess there is no shortage of random things I could name as points of style that all quality tools could check, but probably it would not be very helpful to do that. I think I'll just comment that probably we could just be running tools like this on huge repositories all at once, so it is nice that the tool relies on scripts to avoid having to spend much on tokens, and it would be good to lean into that.

The skill has a /teach where you can suggest things it should be doing and then, if you want, you can ask it to make a PR to the skill repo. I'd be interested in any style or other improvements you think would be helpful. So far I've just been using for my own projects and sphere packing and updating it as I go along.

I think an issue when talking about style is that you can talk about it in finer-and-finer grained detail. For example there is this repo of almost 800 conventions for mathlib code, but if we were to pass this entire file to a model to check every single point against each theorem, it would be running all day. So the trick is maybe to distill these into programmatically checkable conventions that the agent can use a script to implement.

I'll submit a PR if there is anything that I think I can improve about the skill.

Bolton Bailey said:

these into programmatically checkable conventions that the agent can use a script to implement

and then PR as linters upstream, so everyone gets the benefit! :-)
It's really important that AI automation doesn't inhibit writing the actual automation!
Where's the link? I vibe coded something similar myself sometime. I believe @Kim Morrison made something more principled. I would be great if there would be an official linter.
